title: Welcome Wolfgang Smith and Brian Murphy
Wolfgang, do you have any thoughts about the topic of consciousness?
Jack interrupts Wolfgang asking what happened at age 14 that made him an opponent of the current Weltanschauung
Wolfgang briefly touches upon the relation between classical physics and quantum physics
Going deeper into why an atomized worldview is not only untenable, but mathematically impossible
Why horizontal causation cannot account for Complex Specified Information
The scientific worldview is ideology-driven according to Wolfgang
Brian asks Wolfgang to elaborate on where he picked up on Heisenberg and how he got to his resolution to the measurement problem
The ontological distinction between a physical and a corporeal entity, and how that relates to the measurement problem
Why Being cannot be explained in terms of sums of parts, and the difference between quantities and qualities
What Wolfgang would like to convey to university students
Measurement gives Being to particles—which otherwise would be mere potentiae—and the causality you need in order to measure a quantum system cannot take place in time
Where does vertical causality come from?
The tripartite cosmos: the aeviternal (subject to neither time nor space), the intermediary (subject to time, but not space), the corporeal (subject to both time and space)
Wolfgang goes into some depth discussing James’ Gibson paper claiming we see reality ‘as it is’, and why the binding-problem cannot be solved on the corporeal level
Why Wolfgang isn’t familiar with most contemporary thinkers
Why the concept of bifurcation as coined by Alfred Whitehead is ultimately untenable
If Heisenberg—who was the most enlightened, metaphysically—had contemplated non-bifurcation more deeply, he would’ve resolved the leading problems in physics
Audience question by Bad_Mofo: What does Dr. Smith think of Alexander Unzicker’s variable light speed theory (originally from Einstein)?
Audience statement by Couldbeme: Many of the comments Dr. Smith has made, and his attention to Plato, seems to align with ideas we hear from John Vervaeke
Afterwords. Thank you Wolfgang and Brian, and good night.
